issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor declaration in the template header uses parameter types (long, long) while the implementation in the template .cpp defines the constructor with (int, int). This mismatch between declaration and definition in the template will confuse students and can lead to an unresolved symbol if the (long,long) constructor is ever used. The solution repository uses (int, int) in the header, showing the intended signature is int. The inconsistency is structural (signature mismatch between header and implementation) and not an intentional pedagogical omission.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent between declaration and definition in the template. Change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to use int parameters (Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height);) to match the implementation, or change the implementation to use long if long is required project-wide. Prefer aligning with the solution (int,int) for width/height.

issues.description: Constructor parameter type for Bitmap24 is inconsistent between the template header and the implementation/solution. In the template repository header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) the constructor is declared as Bitmap24(long i_width, long i_height); but the implementation in example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height). The solution repository uses int for the constructor parameters. This mismatch of the constructor signature across template header vs. implementation/solution can confuse students mapping the class API to its implementation and may cause build errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bitmap24 constructor signature consistent in the template header to match the implementation and solution. Change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp (TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY) from Bitmap24(long i_width, long i_height); to Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height); so that header and implementation use the same parameter types.
